Unos pasajeros bajan y otros suben.

assumptions: Persons are synthetic and consistent with the Census 2024 margins. They are not microdata.
The station model (L9) is fitted on the baseline. Its scale, classes and profiles do not change.
Travel times are comuna to comuna and lower than survey times. The effect of a time change is an unvalidated sensitivity; the size and direction of its error are unknown.
A mode change does not reach the stations yet: stations use the baseline public share of the home comuna.
Open city for residents: more or fewer residents change the total of workers, with the baseline workers per resident of the comuna.
Station access (L9): a walk within 1,000 m, or else one bus. A closed station does not change the travel minutes between comunas or the job choice.
Students do not choose again.
Trips are display groups of workers, not persons. Departure half hours come from the EOD 2012 survey. Students are not included.

The Census sets walking and cycling totals inside each comuna pair. The 2012 survey distance rule allocates workers within those totals. The engine has no measured response for cycling uptake after a new cycleway.
All values are model values, not measured values.

line_riders: trips to work of workers only (no students, no return trips). A worker can use an added line when a stop with boarding is within 1 km of home and a later stop with alighting is within 1 km of the job (straight line, 80 m per minute). Door-to-door minutes = walk + half the headway + scheduled ride + walk. The added line is a fourth mode alternative with the fitted public-transport minute coefficient and the public residual of the comuna pair, and no mode constant of its own. It competes with the comuna-pair public minutes, not with a person-level public trip. Riders per half hour are capped so the busiest segment carries at most departures × vehicle_capacity (one departure profile for all riders); stop and segment counts are scaled by the same daily served share. Riders do not feed back into station boardings or job choice.
Exploratory station boardings after a transit line edit. The station model uses worker origins, job destinations and baseline public transport shares. Ridership on the edited service is unknown.

Depart comuna points at 08:00 on Monday 13 April 2026 and count arrivals by 11:00. Fixed trips use scheduled boarding calls. Frequency trips use half a headway after arrival while the shifted window permits it.
New or explicitly changed frequency runs at the first stop from 08:00 to 09:00. Changes to stops or ride times reuse the published service starts unless headway changes.
Access and egress use straight-line walks up to 1 km. Stop transfers use straight-line walks up to 300 m.
The graph measures travel between comuna population points. A route must include at least one transit segment. Null means no such route in this graph.
A geometry-only move keeps service times and the stop order. For added stop calls, omitted dwell is zero and boarding and alighting are allowed. The shape follows the selected calls in order.
A line that calls at new stops (outside the GTFS catalog) is not in the comuna graph and changes no comuna-pair minutes. Its riders come from the person-level line rider model.
